title: Image models become easier to find and inspect
summary:
Nanobanana and Seedream gained Enter listings, image responses got usage headers, and their queues got a little less queue-shaped.

Nanobanana and Seedream were added to Enter’s image model and service registries. Image responses also gained headers for the model used, user tier, and completion-image-token count, including when an image is converted or resized.

The two image models’ queue interval dropped from 45 to 30 seconds, with higher per-interval caps for Flower and Nectar users. The `gemini` text model switched to Vertex AI, and queue-full errors gained more detailed monitoring. Two PRs covered the same queue and routing changes.

Flux Kontext and Turbo gained explicit per-image prices, while Flux remains priced at zero. Enter’s Pollen balance display now uses its configured meter, checkout has an explicit success URL, and GPT-5 Chat was added to its text usage registry.

highlights.title: Nanobanana in Enter
highlights.text: Find `nanobanana` in Enter’s image model listings. [View the model](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models?q=nanobanana).

highlights.title: Seedream in Enter
highlights.text: Find `seedream` in Enter’s image model listings. [View the model](https://enter.pollinations.ai/models?q=seedream).

highlights.title: Inspect image response usage
highlights.text: Image responses now include `x-model-used`, `x-user-tier`, and `x-completion-image-tokens` headers, so you can inspect which backend handled a generation and its reported image-token usage. [Explore the API docs](https://gen.pollinations.ai/docs).
